title: Retrospective cost-effectiveness analysis of the treatment of critically ill and seriously injured emergency patients in an emergency department
summary: In this retrospective study, routinely documented data from the patient data management system of the Emergency Department of University Hospital Düsseldorf — PDMS/COPRA — will be analyzed for critically ill non-traumatic and traumatic emergency patients treated in the ED. Emergency patients may either be discharged as outpatients or admitted to different levels of in-hospital care, such as a general ward, an intermediate care unit (IMC), or an intensive care unit (ICU). In some cases, ICU bed capacity may be unavailable due to staffing shortages. In such situations, patients who present to the hospital independently, are referred by general practitioners or specialists, or are brought in by emergency medical services or emergency physicians must be appropriately monitored and treated in the Emergency Department. For this purpose, anonymized data will be analyzed for all treated patients who presented to the Emergency Department of University Hospital Düsseldorf between January 1, 2024, and December 31, 2024. For these patients, associated treatment costs will be analyzed and a cost-effectiveness assessment will be performed. To date, only limited health economic data are available regarding the financial sustainability of different treatment pathways across various levels of care. Such insights may help to bundle resources more effectively from a cost-efficiency perspective, optimize workflows, and thereby improve the care of critically ill emergency patients.
